# Assessment — #491: Standalone OpenCode-compatible portal packages (coordinate with guardian state refactor #433)

> NOTE (2026-07-29): written before the `portals/{discord,slack}` → `packages/portal-{discord,slack}` + `packages/portal-sdk` rename; `portals/…` paths below map to those packages.

_Codebase assessment against 0.13.0-beta.3 (2026-07-12). Effort: **M**._

## Current state (already merged)

A large fraction of the issue is already merged. (1) The "@openpalm/portal-kit" extraction (the issue's M-sized follow-on) is DONE as packages/portal-sdk (runtime.ts, opencode.ts OcClient, oc-events.ts, oc-event-hub.ts, base-portal.ts BasePortal, permissions.ts, render-turn.ts, deliver-buffered.ts — all with colocated *.test.ts). Both portals depend on it via "@openpalm/portal-sdk": "workspace:*" (portals/discord/package.json:21, portals/slack/package.json:21). (2) Publishing is DONE: neither portal package.json has "private": true; .github/release-package-groups.json has units.portals = [packages/portal-sdk, portals/discord, portals/slack]; .github/workflows/release.yml has npm-portal-sdk / npm-discord-portal / npm-slack-portal jobs with the portal-sdk-first DAG ordering (release.yml:495-548), and 0.13.0-beta versions have shipped. (3) NOT done — the architectural crux: client-side session reuse. The coordination with #433 was resolved in the OPPOSITE direction from the issue's proposal: the guardian now owns idempotent session reuse server-side via an in-memory BoundedTtlMap keyed by resolveSessionTarget's cacheKey (packages/guardian/src/session-target.ts, proxy.ts:571-600 "Durable session reuse — the portal's in-memory map was a fragile band-aid"), and the Discord portal explicitly deleted its client cache (portals/discord/src/index.ts:71-72: "Session→thread mapping is now the GUARDIAN's job … no client-side session cache is needed"). BasePortal.forward (base-portal.ts:151-174) calls client.createSession(userId, sessionKey) every turn relying on the x-openpalm-session-key header (opencode.ts:44-58) — against a plain OpenCode server this creates a fresh session per turn, so multi-turn breaks standalone. (4) NOT done — auth UX: portal-sdk only has readRequiredSecretFile (_FILE path indirection, runtime.ts:50-68); no direct-env fallback (OPENCODE_PASSWORD / DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN / SLACK_BOT_TOKEN). BasePortal.secret hard-requires PRINCIPAL_SECRET_FILE (base-portal.ts:116). (5) NOT done — branding: Slack hardcodes "Ask OpenPalm" (index.ts:324,377-378,572) and "OpenPalm on Slack" (index.ts:551); no SLACK_BOT_NAME. (6) NOT done — bin/ CLI entrypoints: neither portal package.json has a "bin" field; the only launcher is containers/portal/portal-entrypoint.ts which imports the class from a baked node_modules and calls new PortalClass().start(). (7) REGRESSION vs the issue's premise: OPENCODE_BASE_URL is now dead code in the BasePortal path — BasePortal always passes baseUrl: `${this.guardianUrl}/oc` with guardianUrl hardcoded to 'http://guardian:8080' (base-portal.ts:80,193), so OcClient's env fallback (opencode.ts:30) is never reached, even though the compose overlay (packages/skeleton/system/stack/portals.compose.yml:15,56) and both READMEs (discord/README.md:43, slack/README.md:48) advertise OPENCODE_BASE_URL. (8) NOT done — READMEs still address the guardian/Compose audience only; no standalone section and no security framing. engines.bun (">=1.0.0") remains on all three packages with TS-source publishing ("files": ["src"], main: src/index.ts) and Bun APIs (Bun.env, Bun.serve) throughout — the Node-compat decision was implicitly resolved as Bun-only but never documented.

## Remaining work

- [ ] Fix the OPENCODE_BASE_URL regression: make BasePortal.guardianUrl env-driven (e.g. read Bun.env.OPENCODE_BASE_URL / GUARDIAN_URL in base-portal.ts, or stop passing an explicit baseUrl so OcClient's existing env fallback at opencode.ts:30 applies). Add a runtime.test.ts/base-portal.test.ts case proving the env var reaches OcClient.
- [ ] Add client-side session reuse to portal-sdk as a standalone fallback: a Map<sessionKey, sessionId> (TTL-pruned) consulted in BasePortal.forward and the streaming paths before createSession; keep sending x-openpalm-session-key as the guardian hint. Decide the mode switch with #433 in mind — e.g. PORTAL_SESSION_REUSE=client|server or detect guardian vs plain OpenCode — and document that behind the guardian the server-side cache (guardian proxy.ts:571) remains authoritative so the two caches don't fight (guardian re-pointing sessions on /clear, DELETE /session eviction).
- [ ] Auth UX: add a readRequiredSecret(envKey) helper in portal-sdk/src/runtime.ts that accepts a direct env var (PRINCIPAL_SECRET / OPENCODE_PASSWORD, DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_BOT_TOKEN, SLACK_APP_TOKEN) with the existing _FILE variant as fallback; adopt it in BasePortal.secret (base-portal.ts:116), discord index.ts:85, slack index.ts:82-86. Keep PRINCIPAL_ID as free-form Basic username (already is, base-portal.ts:191).
- [ ] Branding: replace hardcoded 'Ask OpenPalm' / 'OpenPalm on Slack' strings in portals/slack/src/index.ts (lines 324, 377-378, 551, 572) with a SLACK_BOT_NAME-derived value (default 'OpenPalm'); audit discord for equivalents (help text in commands.ts).
- [ ] CLI entrypoints: add portals/discord/bin/openpalm-discord-portal.ts and portals/slack/bin/openpalm-slack-portal.ts (instantiate + start(), mirroring containers/portal/portal-entrypoint.ts), add "bin" fields and include bin/ in "files" in both package.jsons.
- [ ] Rewrite portals/discord/README.md and portals/slack/README.md for a standalone audience: bunx/bun-install quick start against any OpenCode server, env table (direct-env and _FILE forms, OPENCODE_BASE_URL), explicit Bun-runtime requirement, and the mandated security framing ('runs best behind the OpenPalm guardian; standalone is for personal/small-trusted-team use' — loses per-principal isolation, rate limiting, moderation). Cross-link docs/portals/community-portals.md.
- [ ] Verify and document which OpenCode server versions expose the endpoints the portals use standalone (/permission/{requestID}/reply, /question/{requestID}/reply|reject — currently proxied through the guardian allowlist, guardian proxy.ts:273-336); degrade gracefully or document the minimum @opencode-ai/sdk-compatible server if absent.
- [ ] Record the Bun-runtime decision explicitly (keep engines.bun, publish TS source) or add a Node build target; update issue checklist either way.

## Test strategy

All affected packages use colocated Bun tests (src/*.test.ts). Root runs them via `bun test --no-orphans portals/discord portals/slack packages/portal-sdk ...` (root package.json "test", line 62); packages/portal-sdk also has its own `bun test` script. Test-first: (1) extend packages/portal-sdk/src/runtime.test.ts with readRequiredSecret direct-env + _FILE-fallback cases; (2) extend packages/portal-sdk/src/base-portal.test.ts (existing pattern injects a fake OcClient via createOcClient override) with a case where two forward() calls with the same sessionKey against a client that ignores x-openpalm-session-key reuse one sessionId, and a case proving OPENCODE_BASE_URL reaches OcClient; (3) new packages/portal-sdk/src/session-map.test.ts for the TTL/eviction behavior of the client-side reuse map; (4) extend portals/slack/src/index.test.ts to assert SLACK_BOT_NAME substitution in modal/Home-tab payloads; (5) a bin smoke test can follow containers/portal/start.test.ts style. Run: `bun test packages/portal-sdk portals/discord portals/slack`.

## Dependencies (0.13.0 open issues)

- #433 — the session-continuity split must be settled with the guardian state store work: the guardian already implemented server-side idempotent session reuse (proxy.ts:571, session-target.ts) as in-memory-only state, directly contradicting this issue's client-side proposal; adding a client-side map without agreeing which side is authoritative (and whether #433 Phase 2 persists the reuse cache or only ownership/permission state) risks persisting the same concept in two places and cache-fight bugs on /clear and session eviction.

## Risks

- Dual session caches (portal client-side + guardian server-side BoundedTtlMap) can disagree after guardian /clear or DELETE /session eviction, silently resuming a stale or foreign session — the guardian comment explicitly calls the old portal-side map 'a fragile band-aid', so reintroducing it needs a clear authoritative-side rule.
- Standalone mode loses guardian isolation/rate-limiting/moderation; without the mandated README security framing, publishing bin-wrapped packages makes it easy to expose a shared-session bot to an entire Discord/Slack server.
- The /permission/{requestID}/reply and /question/{requestID}/* endpoints the portals call may not exist on all plain OpenCode server versions — interactive permission/question UX could break standalone even after session reuse is fixed.
- OPENCODE_BASE_URL is documented in READMEs and set by the shipped compose overlay but currently ignored by BasePortal (hardcoded guardianUrl) — any fix changes behavior for existing custom-compose users who set DISCORD_OPENCODE_BASE_URL expecting it to work.
- Published packages are Bun-only TS source (Bun.env/Bun.serve, engines.bun); advertising standalone npm use to a Node audience without deciding the runtime story invites install-and-fail reports.
- release.yml publishes portal-sdk in lockstep with the adapters (workspace:* resolved at pack time) — any new portal-sdk API must land in the same 'portals' release unit or published adapters pin an unpublished sdk version (this exact failure happened at 0.13.0-beta.1, see release.yml:500-504).

## Original issue body

# #491: Standalone OpenCode-compatible portal packages (coordinate with guardian state refactor #433)

## Goal

Publish the portal adapters (`@openpalm/discord-portal`, `@openpalm/slack-portal`) as **standalone npm packages** that work against **any OpenCode server**, not just the OpenPalm guardian. This both serves a "power user / your own OpenCode server" use case and **completes the #434 / #432 thesis** that portal adapters are standard OpenCode-SDK clients (the guardian's value is *validation*, not *transport*).

Spun out of the 0.12.0 portals-rename + build/packaging review. Code is already ~90% there: zero `@openpalm/*` workspace deps (only `@opencode-ai/sdk` + `discord.js`/`@slack/bolt`), env-overridable `OPENCODE_BASE_URL`, no template rendering.

## The architectural crux — and why this coordinates with the guardian state refactor (#433)

The guardian has **two distinct state concerns** today; the portals only need a client-side mirror of the **first**:

1. **Session reuse** — `forward.ts:resolveSessionTarget` maps `${portalId}:${sessionKey}` → an existing OpenCode session (the buffered session cache, `GUARDIAN_SESSION_TTL_MS`). This is what makes multi-turn work. Portals currently rely on the guardian honoring the `x-openpalm-session-key` header to get this; a **plain OpenCode server ignores the header and `session.create()` makes a fresh session every turn** → multi-turn breaks.
2. **Ownership / authz** — `ownership.ts` maps `sessionId → principal` (+ `requestID → principal` for permissions) for per-principal isolation. Pure guardian concern; no standalone equivalent.

**Proposed direction:** move session-reuse **client-side into the portal** (a `Map<threadKey, sessionId>`, optionally locally persisted). Then:
- Portals work against ANY OpenCode endpoint (standalone) AND behind the guardian.
- `x-openpalm-session-key` becomes an **optional guardian hint** (for the guardian's durable, cross-restart, cross-principal reuse) rather than the mechanism multi-turn depends on — a cleaner "standard OpenCode client" contract.
- **This narrows #433 Phase 2**: with reuse client-side, the guardian's durable state is scoped to **ownership/authz + permission ownership** (and cross-restart session continuity as an optimization), not the session-reuse cache. #433 Phase 2 and this issue should be designed together so we don't persist the same concept in two places.

## Coordination checklist

- [ ] **#433 (guardian state store, Phase 2)** — decide the split: client-side session reuse (portal) vs durable ownership (guardian). Scope #433 Phase 2 to ownership/permission persistence accordingly; document `x-openpalm-session-key` as an optional optimization.
- [ ] **#487 (A2A server)** — the A2A `contextId → sessionId` mapping is the same shape as portal session reuse; align the contract so all three front ends (portal/OpenCode-proxy/A2A) treat session continuity consistently.
- [ ] **#434 / #432 (adapters as standard OpenCode-SDK clients)** — this issue is the concrete completion of that thesis for the two first-party portals.

## Standalone packaging gaps (from the investigation)

- [ ] **Session reuse client-side** (the one architectural gap above) — ~20 lines/portal, or in a shared kit.
- [ ] **Auth UX** — `readRequiredSecret()` accepting a direct env var (e.g. `OPENCODE_PASSWORD`, `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`) with `_FILE` fallback (keeps Compose-secrets working). Against plain OpenCode the single Basic password is the auth; `PRINCIPAL_ID` becomes a free-form username.
- [ ] **Branding** — Slack hardcodes "Ask OpenPalm" / "OpenPalm on Slack" (modal titles, Home tab) → make configurable (`SLACK_BOT_NAME`).
- [ ] **CLI entrypoints** — `bin/` wrappers + `bin` field (the container entrypoint instantiates the class today).
- [ ] **Extract `@openpalm/portal-kit`** (M, follow-on) — `runtime.ts` / `oc-events.ts` / `OcClient` / session-map are byte-identical across discord+slack; extract to one shared package (also the home for the client-side session-reuse logic).
- [ ] **Publish** — flip `"private": true` → false on both; add `publish-npm-package` steps; reconcile `release-package-groups.json` (`units.portals`). Decide the **Bun-runtime requirement** (`engines.bun`) — it narrows the Node audience; consider a Node-compatible build target.
- [ ] **Docs** — rewrite both `portals/*/README.md` for a standalone audience.

## Security framing (must be explicit in docs)

Pointing a portal straight at OpenCode loses the guardian's per-principal **isolation**, **rate limiting**, and **content moderation** — every user in a server shares one session namespace. Frame as: *"Runs best behind the OpenPalm guardian (or another auth/rate-limiting reverse proxy). Standalone is for personal / small-trusted-team use against your own OpenCode server."*

## Effort

First shippable increment: **S** (~half a day) — session-reuse + auth UX + branding + `bin/` + `private:false` + publish steps + READMEs. The `@openpalm/portal-kit` extraction is a separate **M**. Recommend doing the **session-reuse / state split with #433** first so the guardian and portal don't diverge.

Related: #433, #487, #434, #432, #436.
